answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because hollow only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, crystal is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any relic approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
